answer: Admission is capped at 3 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm thus spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the vertex quota and the tide admission check. Because the ember audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 25 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
